updates.summary: A new smartphone app for reporting side effects to the Yellow Card Scheme has now launched.

updates.title: Letters sent to healthcare professionals in June 2015
updates.summary: Last month, letters sent included one for the oral anticoagulant edoxaban.

updates.title: Latanoprost (Xalatan): increased reporting of eye irritation since reformulation
updates.summary: Advise patients to tell their health professional if they experience severe eye irritation.

updates.title: Denosumab (Xgeva▼, Prolia); intravenous bisphosphonates: osteonecrosis of the jaw—further measures to minimise risk
updates.summary: Patient reminder cards about the risk of osteonecrosis of the jaw are being introduced; denosumab 120 mg is now contraindicated in patients with unhealed lesions from dental or oral surgery.

updates.title: Survey of medicines safety communications
updates.summary: Please complete our survey on how we communicate medicines safety issues.

updates.title: SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin): risk of diabetic ketoacidosis
updates.summary: Test for raised ketones in patients with acidosis symptoms, even if plasma glucose levels are near-normal.

updates.title: Intrauterine contraception: uterine perforation—updated information on risk factors
updates.summary: The most important risk factors for uterine perforation are insertion during lactation and insertion in the 36 weeks after giving birth. Before inserting an IUS or IUD, inform women of the risk and the symptoms of perforation.

updates.title: Hormonal pregnancy tests and birth defects: call for evidence
updates.summary: A group of independent experts will review all evidence provided; we will publish a report of the group’s findings.

updates.title: High-dose ibuprofen (≥2400mg/day): small increase in cardiovascular risk
updates.summary: EU review confirms that the cardiovascular risk of high-dose ibuprofen (≥2400mg/day) is similar to COX 2 inhibitors and diclofenac.

updates.title: Sofosbuvir with daclatasvir; sofosbuvir and ledipasvir: risks of severe bradycardia and heart block when taken with amiodarone
updates.summary: Avoid concomitant use of amiodarone with ledipasvir-sofosbuvir (Harvoni▼), and amiodarone with sofosbuvir (Sovaldi▼) and daclatasvir (Daklinza▼), unless other antiarrhythmics cannot be given.

updates.title: Pomalidomide (Imnovid▼): risks of cardiac failure, interstitial lung disease and hepatotoxicity
updates.summary: New monitoring instructions to detect these side effects as soon as possible.

updates.title: Letters sent to healthcare professionals in April 2015
updates.summary: Last month, letters were sent regarding ketoprofen gel, fingolimod (Gilenya▼) and efavirenz (Sustiva).

updates.title: Epoetin beta (NeoRecormon): increased risk of retinopathy in preterm infants cannot be excluded
updates.summary: Possible increased risk of retinopathy with epoetin beta in premature infants calls for careful consideration of options for preventing anaemia of prematurity.

updates.title: Letters sent to healthcare professionals in March 2015
updates.summary: Last month, letters were sent regarding ketoconazole HRA and radium-223 dichloride (Xofigo).

updates.title: Hydroxyzine (Atarax, Ucerax): risk of QT interval prolongation and Torsade de Pointes
updates.summary: The maximum adult daily dose of hydroxyzine is now 100 mg. Do not prescribe hydroxyzine to people with a prolonged QT interval or risk factors for QT interval prolongation.

updates.title: High strength, fixed combination and biosimilar insulin products: minimising the risk of medication error
updates.summary: Several new high strength insulin products are now on the market. The European Medicines Agency is consulting on guidance to minimise the risk of medication error.

updates.title: Codeine for cough and cold: restricted use in children
updates.summary: Do not use codeine in children under 12 as it is associated with a risk of respiratory side effects. Codeine is not recommended for adolescents (12 to 18) who have problems with breathing.

updates.title: Report misleading medicines advertisements
updates.summary: If you are concerned about advertising you see for a medicine, please report it to MHRA or the industry self-regulatory body.

updates.title: Ferumoxytol (Rienso) intravenous iron no longer available for use
updates.summary: The licence-holder of ferumoxytol has voluntarily withdrawn it from the UK market for commercial reasons.

updates.title: Dimethyl fumarate (Tecfidera): fatal PML in an MS patient with severe, prolonged lymphopenia
updates.summary: Check full blood counts before prescribing dimethyl fumarate and then every 6 to 12 months. Stop treatment immediately if you suspect progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.

updates.title: Corticosteroids e-learning module launched
updates.summary: The new module helps clinicians understand how to identify, manage and avoid side effects when using corticosteroids.

updates.title: Tiotropium delivered via Respimat compared with Handihaler: no significant difference in mortality in TIOSPIR trial
updates.summary: Take the risk of cardiovascular side effects into account when prescribing tiotropium delivered via Respimat or Handihaler to patients with certain cardiac conditions, who were excluded from clinical trials of tiotropium (including TIOSPIR).

updates.title: Nitrofurantoin now contraindicated in most patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of less than 45 ml/min/1.73m2
updates.summary: A short course (3 to 7 days) may be used with caution in certain patients with an eGFR of 30 to 44 ml/min/1.73m2

updates.title: Letters sent to healthcare professionals since November 2014
updates.summary: Since November 2014, letters were sent regarding vismodegib (Erivedge ▼), chlorhexidine solutions, carbocisteine oral liquid (Mucodyne Paediatric 125mg/5ml), regadenoson (Rapiscan), a parenteral nutrition emulsion (Triomel), and telavancin (Vibativ▼).

updates.title: INOmax (nitric oxide) cylinders: valve defect might stop gas delivery early in some cylinders
updates.summary: While this defect is still being investigated, we remind you to always have a full spare cylinder loaded on the delivery device so the cylinders can be switched without delay.

updates.title: Drugs and driving: blood concentration limits set for certain drugs
updates.summary: We remind you that a new offence will be enforced from 2 March 2015 in England and Wales. Talk to patients who are on medicines with potential to impair driving and discuss the patient leaflet advice.

updates.title: Yellow Card extended to include devices, counterfeits and defective medicines
updates.summary: We have simplified our medicine and device incident report systems by bringing them all under the Yellow Card Scheme.

updates.title: Ustekinumab (Stelara): risk of exfoliative dermatitis
updates.summary: If you suspect exfoliative dermatitis caused by an adverse drug reaction to ustekinumab, stop treatment.

updates.title: Oral diclofenac no longer available without prescription
updates.summary: Oral diclofenac is associated with a small increased risk of cardiovascular side effects and is therefore no longer available over the counter.

updates.title: Mycophenolate mofetil (CellCept) and mycophenolic acid: risk of hypogammaglobulinaemia and risk of bronchiectasis
updates.summary: Measure serum immunoglobulin levels if recurrent infections develop. Consider bronchiectasis or pulmonary fibrosis if patients develop persistent respiratory symptoms.

updates.title: Medicines related to valproate: risk of abnormal pregnancy outcomes
updates.summary: Children exposed in utero to valproate are at a high risk of serious developmental disorders (in up to 30-40% of cases) and/or congenital malformations (in approximately 10% of cases).

updates.title: Aceclofenac (Preservex): updated cardiovascular advice in line with diclofenac and COX-2 inhibitors
updates.summary: Aceclofenac is now contraindicated in patients with certain established cardiovascular diseases.

updates.title: Veletri (epoprostenol) powder for solution for infusion: incompatibilities with some models of administration devices
updates.summary: Reports of reconstituted solution leaking from some models of extension sets and pumps.

updates.title: Ivabradine (Procoralan) in the symptomatic treatment of angina: risk of cardiac side effects
updates.summary: New advice to minimise risk

updates.title: Isotretinoin (Roaccutane): reminder of possible risk of psychiatric disorders
updates.summary: Warn patients and family, monitor patients for signs of depression

updates.title: Hydroxyethyl starch intravenous infusions
updates.summary: To be used only in patients with acute blood loss and when crystalloids alone are not sufficient.

updates.title: Hydrogen peroxide: reminder of risk of gas embolism when used in surgery
updates.summary: Do not use in closed body cavities or on deep or large wounds.

updates.title: Zolpidem: risk of drowsiness and reduced driving ability
updates.summary: Taking zolpidem is associated with a risk of impaired driving ability the next day.

updates.title: Yellow Card: update to form
updates.summary: Reporting suspected adverse reactions experienced by the woman or child associated with medicines taken during pregnancy.

updates.title: Yellow Card Scheme update: seasonal flu vaccines in children
updates.summary: Report of febrile promptly.

updates.title: Yasmin: risk of venous thromboembolism higher than levonorgestrel-containing pills
updates.summary: Risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) for drospirenone-containing combined oral contraceptives (COCs), including Yasmin, is higher than for levonorgestrel-containing COCs.

updates.title: Warfarin: product information to be amended to give clearer, up-to-date advice
updates.summary: We continue to receive a substantial number of serious and fatal adverse event reports for warfarin through our Yellow Card Scheme.

updates.title: Voriconazole: reminder of risk of liver toxicity, phototoxicity, and squamous cell carcinoma
updates.summary: Test liver function before and during treatment and tell patients to avoid sunlight exposure.

updates.title: Vivaglobin solution for subcutaneous injection: rare risk of thromboembolic events
updates.summary: Where possible, use an appropriate alternative therapy for patients at increased risk of thrombosis.

updates.title: Vimpat▼ (lacosamide) 15 mg/mL syrup: recall due to quality defect
updates.summary: Recall will begin in September 2011 to allow sufficient time for patients to be switched to suitable alternatives.

updates.title: Vigabatrin for infantile spasms: risk of movement disorders and MRI abnormalities
updates.summary: If new movement disorders occur during treatment consider dose reduction or a gradual discontinuation of treatment in consultation with specialist advice.

updates.title: Varenicline and suicidal behaviour: cohort study provides some reassurance
updates.summary: The study found no clear evidence that varenicline was associated with an increased risk of fatal or non-fatal self-harm.

updates.title: Unlicensed imported vitamin D (colecalciferol) capsules: potential peanut oil and soya oil allergens
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should be aware that these capsules contain potential allergens.

updates.title: Tumour necrosis factor alpha inhibitors
updates.summary: Risk of tuberculosis - screen all patients before starting treatment and monitor them closely.

updates.title: Tredaptive (combined niacin-laropiprant): no longer for prescribing
updates.summary: Preliminary HPS2-THRIVE trial failed to show benefit outweighs risks

updates.title: Treating paracetamol overdose with intravenous acetylcysteine: new guidance
updates.summary: New simplified guidance on treating paracetamol overdose with intravenous acetylcysteine including an updated treatment nomogram.

updates.title: Transdermal fentanyl “patches”: reminder of potential for life-threatening harm from accidental exposure, particularly in children
updates.summary: We remind you to provide clear information to patients and caregivers regarding risk of accidental patch transfer and ingestion of patches, and need for appropriate disposal of patches.

updates.title: Traditional Chinese medicines containing lei gong teng (tripterygium wilfordii)
updates.summary: Risk of serious side effects on fertility, the liver, kidneys, immune system, blood, and heart.

updates.title: Toremifene (Fareston): risk of QT prolongation
updates.summary: Toremifene (fareston) is associated with a dose-dependent risk of QT prolongation.

updates.title: Topical ketoprofen: reminder on risk of photosensitivity reactions
updates.summary: European Medicines Agency says further measures should be put in place to minimise the risk of adverse skin reactions.

updates.title: Topical ketoprofen: reminder on risk of photo-sensitivity reactions
updates.summary: A reminder for those who use topical ketoprofen to avoid direct sunlight, ultraviolet rays, sunbeds or sunlamps.

updates.title: Tolvaptan (Samsca▼): risk of liver injury
updates.summary: liver-function testing recommended in patients with symptoms that may indicate liver injury.

updates.title: Tolvaptan (Samsca▼): over-rapid increase in serum sodium risking serious neurological events
updates.summary: Careful monitoring of serum sodium important, co-administration of other drugs that may increase serum sodium not recommended.

updates.title: Tiotropium
updates.summary: Safety studies of Spiriva Respimat▼

updates.title: Time to report
updates.summary: A reminder to healthcare professionals to fill out Yellow Card reports.

updates.title: Tigecycline (Tygacil▼): increased mortality in clinical trials
updates.summary: Use only when other antibiotics are unsuitable

updates.title: Tibolone: benefit-risk balance
updates.summary: Increased risk of stroke in older women should be taken into account in prescribing decisions.

updates.title: The Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee
updates.summary: Strengthening surveillance of medicines throughout the EU

updates.title: The Black Triangle Scheme (▼ or ▼*)
updates.summary: Continued monitoring of medicines with a black triangle status.

updates.title: Thalidomide: risk of second primary malignancies
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should consider this risk when deciding whether to treat patients with thalidomide monitor for the occurrence of these conditions.

updates.title: Thalidomide: risk of arterial and venous thromboembolism
updates.summary: Increased risk of arterial thromboembolism, including myocardial infarction and cerebrovascular events for patients treated with thalidomide.

updates.title: Teva levothyroxine 100 microgram tablets: suspension of marketing authorisation
updates.summary: Following a review by the Commission on Human Medicines (CHM), the marketing authorisation (licence) for levothyroxine 100 microgram tablets manufactured by Teva has been suspended.

updates.title: Temsirolimus: severe hypersensitivity reactions during infusion
updates.summary: Severe infusion-related hypersensitivity reactions have occurred in patients receiving temsirolimus.

updates.title: Temozolomide: risk of hepatic injury, including fatal hepatic failure—updated warnings and monitoring guidance
updates.summary: Liver function should be tested before and during treatment with temozolomide.

updates.title: Telbivudine and pegylated interferon: risk of peripheral neuropathy
updates.summary: Patients who take telbivudine and pegylated interferon are at increased risk of peripheral neuropathy and should stop taking both medicines if symptoms occur.

updates.title: Tazocin (piperacillin/tazobactam): new formulation
updates.summary: Tazocin (piperacillin/tazobactam) has been reformulated to meet European Pharmacopoeia requirements on particle size.

updates.title: Tamoxifen for breast cancer
updates.summary: Drug interactions involving CYP2D6, genetic variants, and variability in clinical response

updates.title: Talc for pleurodesis: adverse effects
updates.summary: We have recently advised that talc preparations for pleurodesis are to be considered as medicinal products.

updates.title: Tacrolimus ointment (Protopic): possible risk of malignancies including lymphomas and skin cancers
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals reminded that tacrolimus may be associated with possible risk of malignancy.

updates.title: Systemic fusidic acid and interaction with statins
updates.summary: There is a risk of rhabdomyolysis if Systemic fusidic acid (Fucidin) is given with statins.

updates.title: Strontium ranelate: cardiovascular risk
updates.summary: Restricted indication and new monitoring requirements.

updates.title: Stavudine (Zerit): increased risk of potentially severe adverse effects
updates.summary: Stavudine should only be used when there are no appropriate alternatives, and for the shortest possible time.

updates.title: Statins: updated adverse reaction information in patient leaflets
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should be aware of the updated information so they can discuss it with new and existing patients.

updates.title: Statins: risk of hyperglycaemia and diabetes
updates.summary: Statin use may be associated with a level of hyperglycaemia in some patients where formal diabetes care is appropriate.

updates.title: Statins: interactions, and updated advice for atorvastatin
updates.summary: Detailed recommendations for dose restrictions when used with some other drugs as interactions may increase the risk of adverse effects, or reduce the effectiveness of statin treatment.

updates.title: Statins: benefits and risks
updates.summary: Statins (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors) are widely used medicines for patients with lipid disorders and in the primary and secondary prevention of heart attack and stroke.

updates.title: St John’s wort: interaction with hormonal contraceptives, including implants
updates.summary: St John’s wort interacts with hormonal contraceptives reducing the effectiveness and increasing the risk of unplanned pregnancy.

updates.title: SSRIs and SNRIs: risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension in the newborn
updates.summary: Epidemiological data suggest that the use of SSRIs in pregnancy, particularly in the later stages, may increase the risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension in the newborn. Healthcare professionals are encouraged to enquire about the use of SSRIs and SNRIs, particularly in women in the later stages of pregnancy. Close observation of neonates exposed to SSRIs or SNRIs for signs of PPHN is recommended after birth

updates.title: Sprayable fibrin sealants (Evicel, Tisseel and Artiss): updated guidance
updates.summary: Updated guidance on minimising risk of life-threatening and fatal air embolism.

updates.title: Sodium valproate: Risk of neurodevelopmental delay in children following maternal use
updates.summary: Not for use in pregnancy unless there is no effective alternative.

updates.title: Smoking and smoking cessation: clinically significant interactions with commonly used medicines
updates.summary: Doses of theophylline, fluvoxamine, caffeine, coumarins including warfarin and the antipsychotics clozapine and olanzapine may have to be altered.

updates.title: Sitaxentan (Thelin▼): worldwide withdrawal from the market
updates.summary: Sitaxentan (Thelin▼) withdrawn due to hepatotoxicity.

updates.title: Sirolimus: different immunoassays for therapeutic drug monitoring—risk of incorrect dose adjustment
updates.summary: Needs a summary

updates.title: Simvastatin: updated advice on drug interactions
updates.summary: Updated contraindications and maximum dose recommendations when taken with a number of other medicines.

updates.title: Simvastatin: increased risk of myopathy at high dose (80 mg)
updates.summary: There is an increased risk of myopathy associated with high-dose (80 mg) simvastatin. The 80-mg dose should be considered only in patients with severe hypercholesterolaemia and high risk of cardiovascular complications who have not achieved their treatment goals on lower doses, when the benefits are expected to outweigh the potential risks

updates.title: Simvastatin: dose limitations with concomitant amlodipine or diltiazem
updates.summary: The maximum recommended dose for simvastatin in conjunction with amlodipine and diltiazem is now 20 mg/day.

updates.title: Sibutramine: suspension of EU licences recommended
updates.summary: Evidence indicates risks outweigh benefits.

updates.title: Short-acting β2 agonists: restricted use for tocolysis in premature labour
updates.summary: Use has been restricted to 48 hours’ maximum parenteral use under specialist supervision, after a European safety review.

updates.title: Serious and fatal overdose of fentanyl patches
updates.summary: MHRA has received reports of unintentional overdose of fentanyl due to dosing errors, accidental exposure, and exposure of the patch to a heat source.

updates.title: Seasonal flu vaccines
updates.summary: No evidence of increased risk of febrile convulsions in children.

updates.title: Saquinavir: update on potential risk of arrhythmia
updates.summary: Saquinavir at a reduced dose for the first week of treatment

updates.title: Rotigotine patches: lifting of prescribing restrictions
updates.summary: Cold-chain storage and distribution system now been fully implemented by manufacturer.

updates.title: Rosiglitazone: recommended withdrawal from clinical use
updates.summary: Suspension of the marketing authorisations of rosiglitazone (Avandia, Avandamet) recommended across the European Union.

updates.title: Roflumilast (Daxas▼): risk of suicidal behaviour
updates.summary: Avoid use in patients with previous or existing psychiatric symptoms and discontinue treatment if new or worsening psychiatric symptoms occur.

updates.title: Rivastigmine (Exelon) transdermal patch: risk of medication errors
updates.summary: Medication errors and inappropriate use of the rivastigmine transdermal patch have been reported, some of which resulted in overdose. Healthcare professionals should be aware of the correct use of rivastigmine, and should advise patients and caregivers as outlined in this article.

updates.title: Rituximab: screen for hepatitis B virus before treatment
updates.summary: Screening for hepatitis B virus is now recommended in all patients (not only those at risk of this infection) before starting treatment for all indications.

updates.title: Rituximab: progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy in a patient
updates.summary: A case of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) with a fatal outcome was reported in a patient with rheumatoid arthritis who had not previously received treatment with methotrexate or a TNF antagonist.

updates.title: Risperidone and paliperidone: risk of intraoperative floppy iris syndrome in patients undergoing cataract surgery
updates.summary: Cases of intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) during cataract surgery have been reported in patients taking the atypical antipsychotics risperidone or paliperidone.

updates.title: Rifadin infusion (rifampicin): new solvent formulation and changes to compatible diluents
updates.summary: The solvent used in the preparation of Rifadin infusion has been reformulated. As a result, it can only be diluted with either dextrose 5% solution or sodium chloride 0·9% solution

updates.title: Review on long-acting β2 agonists for asthma
updates.summary: Long-acting β2 agonists (LABA) should only be prescribed in conjunction with inhaled corticosteroids for the treatment of moderate to severe asthma.

updates.title: Retigabine (Trobalt▼): indication restricted to last-line use and new monitoring requirements
updates.summary: Reports of pigment changes in ocular tissue, skin, lips or nails.

updates.title: Reporting suspected adverse drug reactions to vaccines and biological medicines
updates.summary: The non-identical nature of biological medicines and vaccines means it is very important that safety surveillance is carried out on a brand/product-specific basis.

updates.title: Report adverse reactions associated with intra-articular use of local anaesthetics
updates.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has received 35 reports of chondrolysis involving patients given continuous intra-articular infusions of local anaesthetics.

updates.title: Recombinant human erythropoietins: treating anaemia in cancer
updates.summary: Patients with cancer who received recombinant human erythropoietins in clinical trials had an increased risk of tumour progression and reduced overall survival compared with study controls.

updates.title: Recombinant human erythropoietins: new advice for prescribing
updates.summary: Over-correction of haemoglobin concentration may increase the risk of death and serious cardiovascular events in patients with chronic kidney disease; it may increase the risk of thrombosis and related complications in patients with cancer.

updates.title: Recognised safety profile of flu antivirals and vaccines confirmed
updates.summary: No unexpected new safety issues have been identified from Yellow Card reports.

updates.title: Recent drug-name confusion
updates.summary: Please be vigilant as life-threatening errors may occur

updates.title: Reboxetine: benefit-risk balance reviewed
updates.summary: A UK and Europe-wide review of available efficacy and safety data confirmed that reboxetine has benefit over placebo in its authorised indication.

updates.title: Quinine: not to be used routinely for nocturnal leg cramps
updates.summary: Quinine should only be considered when cramps cause regular disruption of sleep.

updates.title: Public perception of herbal medicines
updates.summary: In 2008 MHRA commissioned Ipsos MORI to research the public’s perception of herbal medicines, the findings may help doctors and pharmacists when considering how to advise patients.

updates.title: Public consultation on new pharmacovigilance legislation
updates.summary: How to comment on new pharmacovigilance legislation.

updates.title: Pseudoephedrine and ephedrine: update on managing risk of misuse
updates.summary: The Commission on Human Medicines recommend that existing levels of monitoring, education, and awareness measures by pharmacists should be maintained.

updates.title: Pseudoephedrine and ephedrine: nasal decongestants
updates.summary: How to reduce risk of illicit use.

updates.title: Pseudoephedrine and ephedrine: managing risk of misuse
updates.summary: Update on managing risk of misuse.

updates.title: Proton pump inhibitors in long-term use: reports of hypomagnesaemia
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should consider measuring magnesium levels before starting PPI treatment and repeat measurements periodically during prolonged treatment.

updates.title: Proton pump inhibitors in long-term use: increased risk of fracture
updates.summary: Recent epidemiological evidence of an increased risk of fracture with long-term use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs).

updates.title: Prasugrel (Efient▼): rare but serious hypersensitivity reactions
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should be aware of this risk when prescribing prasugrel.

updates.title: Prasugrel (Efient): increased risk of bleeding
updates.summary: New clinical trial information is available on the timing of the loading dose of prasugrel when used in patients with unstable angina or non-ST segment elevation myocardial infarction.

updates.title: Ponatinib (Iclusig▼): risk of vascular occlusive events
updates.summary: Available evidence shows that the risk of blood vessel blockage with ponatinib is likely to be dose-dependent, however the data are insufficient to recommend reducing the ponatinib dose.

updates.title: Pneumovax II: tolerability of re-vaccination
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should advise patients who need re-vaccination with Pneumovax II to expect a more intense reaction than after their first vaccination.

updates.title: Piroxicam: new restrictions, including specialist initiation
updates.summary: Systemic piroxicam should be initiated only by specialists as a second-line treatment for arthritis, with patients who currently take piroxicam reassessed at a routine appointment.

updates.title: Piperacillin/tazobactam: compatibility of generics is different from brand leader (tazocin)
updates.summary: Generic piperacillin/tazobactam products have different compatibilities with other medicines compared with tazocin, raising a risk of serious medication errors.

updates.title: Pioglitazone: risk of bladder cancer
updates.summary: Use of pioglitazone is associated with a small increased risk of bladder cancer. Healthcare professionals should be aware of new warnings and precautions for use in at-risk patients

updates.title: PIL of the month: Durogesic D Trans Transdermal Patch
updates.summary: Best practice example of a patient information leaflet.

updates.title: Phenytoin: risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome associated with HLA-B*1502 allele in patients of Thai or Han Chinese ethnic origin
updates.summary: If patients are known to be HLA-B*1502-positive, phenytoinshould be avoided when alternative therapy can be given.

updates.title: Parenteral amphotericin B: fatal overdose risk due to confusion between lipid-based and non-lipid-based formulations
updates.summary: There is a potential risk of fatal overdose due to confusion between lipid-based and non-lipid-based formulations of parenteral amphotericin B. These formulations are not interchangeable: prescribers, pharmacists, and nurses need to be fully aware of the formulation being used and the associated dose regimen

updates.title: Paraffin-based treatments: risk of fire hazard
updates.summary: Paraffin based products such as white soft paraffin can set on fire easily.

updates.title: Paracetamol: updated dosing for children to be introduced
updates.summary: Updated dosing for paediatric paracetamol liquids has been developed to ensure children receive the optimum dose for their age.

updates.title: Paracetamol: reminder of updated dosing recommendations for children
updates.summary: Reminder that paediatric paracetamol liquids had been developed to ensure children receive optimum dosing for their age.

updates.title: Panitumumab (Vectibix): serious hypersensitivity reactions
updates.summary: New reports of serious hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis) in patients receiving panitumumab, some of which were fatal.

updates.title: Panitumumab (Vectibix): risk of necrotising fasciitis
updates.summary: Five cases of necrotising fasciitis have been reported in patients treated with panitumumab in combination with chemotherapy.

updates.title: Panitumumab: treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer
updates.summary: Importance of establishing wildtype RAS (KRAS and NRAS) status before treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer.

updates.title: Pandemic vaccines and antivirals: safety review
updates.summary: Outline of the safety experience of these medicines in the UK from our proactive safety monitoring strategy.

updates.title: Pabrinex: allergic reactions
updates.summary: Rare occurrence of serious allergic reactions should not preclude use of parenteral thiamine in patients who need treatment by this route of administration.

updates.title: Over-the-counter painkillers containing codeine or dihydrocodeine
updates.summary: The tighter controls being introduced to minimise risk of overuse and or addiction of painkillers containing codeine or dihydrocodeine.

updates.title: Over-the-counter cough and cold medicines for children
updates.summary: Advice on how to use cough and cold medicines safely for children under 12 years.

updates.title: Oseltamivir (Tamiflu): update to Patient Information Leaflet
updates.summary: There is no known interaction between oseltamivir and aspirin but aspirin must not be given to anyone younger than 16 year.

updates.title: Oseltamivir (Tamiflu): changed concentration and dosing dispenser of oral suspension
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should advise patients and/or carers of the changes in the dose, packaging, dose dispenser and leaflet.

updates.title: Orlistat: theoretical interaction with antiretroviral HIV medicines
updates.summary: Initiate orlistat treatment only after careful consideration of the possible impact on efficacy of antiretroviral HIV medicines.

updates.title: Orlistat safety update
updates.summary: A recent Europe-wide review of the safety information for alli has led to a number of updates, which bring the product information in line with that for Xenical.

updates.title: Orciprenaline sulphate (Alupent): withdrawal due to unfavourable benefit-risk profile
updates.summary: Patients who require a liquid oral formulation of a β-agonist should be switched to a more-selective short-acting β2-agonist such as salbutamol or terbutaline.

updates.title: Orciprenaline sulphate (Alupent): reminder of withdrawal from the market
updates.summary: Patients should be transferred to alternative bronchodilator therapy.

updates.title: Oral tacrolimus products: prescribe and dispense by brand name only, to minimise the risk of inadvertent switching between products, which has been associated with reports of toxicity and graft rejection
updates.summary: The growing number of oral tacrolimus products available on the market increases the potential for inadvertent switching between products, which has been associated with reports of toxicity and graft rejection. Therefore, to ensure maintenance of therapeutic response when a patient is stabilised on a particular brand, oral tacrolimus products should be prescribed and dispensed by brand name only. If a prescriber considers that switching a patient to a different brand of oral tacrolimus would be of benefit, the change requires careful supervision and therapeutic monitoring by an appropriate specialist

updates.title: Oral salicylate gels: not for use in those younger than age 16 years
updates.summary: Topical oral salicylate gels are no longer indicated for people younger than 16 years for pain associated with infant teething, orthodontic devices, cold sores, or mouth ulcers.

updates.title: Oral retinoids: pregnancy prevention—reminder of measures to minimise teratogenic risk
updates.summary: The risk of foetal malformation with oral retinoids is extremely high, even when used at a low dose or for a short time during pregnancy. All oral retinoids have an associated Pregnancy Prevention Programme (PPP), which is supported by educational material for prescribers, pharmacists, and patients. Women of child-bearing potential should have pregnancy excluded before starting treatment. While taking these medicines, one—or preferably two—different forms of contraception must be consistently used

updates.title: Oral ketoconazole: do not prescribe or use for fungal infections—risk of liver injury outweighs benefits
Oral bisphosphonates: oesophageal cancer risk—insufficient evidence of a link
updates.summary: Insufficient evidence to confirm a link between oral bisphosphonate use and an increased risk of oesophageal cancer.

updates.title: Oral anticancer medicines: risk of incorrect dosing
updates.summary: Advice for healthcare professionals on potentially fatal outcomes of oral anticancer medicines if they are not prescribed, dispensed or administered properly.

updates.title: Onsenal▼ (Celecoxib) withdrawn from EU market
updates.summary: Onsenal▼ (celecoxib) is no longer approved in Europe for the reduction of intestinal polyps in familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP).

updates.title: Ondansetron (Zofran): important new intravenous dose restriction
updates.summary: New maximum single intravenous dose of ondansetron for the management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) restricted due to risk of QTc prolongation.

updates.title: Ondansetron for intravenous use: posology in patients age 65 years or older
updates.summary: New advice on dilution and administration in patients age 65 years or older refers only to the indication for prevention of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.

updates.title: Ondansetron for intravenous use: dose-dependent QT interval prolongation
updates.summary: New specific guidance on dose-dependent prolongation of QTc with ondansetron.

updates.title: Omalizumab: potential risk of arterial thrombotic events
updates.summary: Prescribers should be vigilant for possible thrombotic adverse reactions.

updates.title: Off-label or unlicensed use of medicines: prescribers’ responsibilities
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals may have more responsibility to accurately prescribe an unlicensed medicine or an off-label medicine than when they prescribe a medicine within the terms of its licence.

updates.title: Off-label intraocular use of recombinant tissue plasminogen activator
updates.summary: Risk of intraocular lens opacification.

updates.title: Ofatumumab: screen for hepatitis B virus before treatment
updates.summary: Patients with active infection with this virus should not be treated with ofatumumab.

updates.title: Ofatumumab▼: reminder of risk of serious and fatal infusion reactions
updates.summary: Serious and fatal infusion reactions have occurred with ofatumumab and other anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies. We remind you to always give premedication before each ofatumumab infusion. If a severe reaction occurs, interrupt ofatumumab infusion and treat the reaction.

updates.title: Octagam intravenous immunoglobulin 5% and 10%: licence suspensions lifted
updates.summary: Suspension of the licences (marketing authorisations) for Octagam (intravenous human normal immunoglobulin 5% and 10%) lifted.

updates.title: NSAIDs and coxibs: balancing of cardiovascular and gastrointestinal risks
updates.summary: Patients should use the lowest effective dose, and the shortest duration of treatment necessary to control symptoms.

updates.title: Norfloxacin: restricted use in urinary infections
updates.summary: The European Medicines Agency (EMA) has concluded that oral fluoroquinolone norfloxacin (Utinor) shouldn't be used to treat acute or chronic, complicated pyelonephritis.

updates.title: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs): reminder on renal failure and impairment
updates.summary: You should take caution when you use NSAIDs in patients with renal impairment or are at risk.

updates.title: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs): cardiovascular risks
updates.summary: Further evidence that the cardiovascular risk with diclofenac is higher than other non-selective NSAIDs and similar to the selective COX-2 inhibitors.

updates.title: Nitrous oxide: neurological and haematological toxic effects
updates.summary: Toxic effects can occur with nitrous oxide especially with prolonged use.

updates.title: Nicotine replacement therapy and harm reduction
updates.summary: Extension of the indication for nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) to include harm reduction.

updates.title: Nicorandil: risk of gastrointestinal ulceration
updates.summary: Nicorandil is associated with a risk of gastrointestinal ulceration including perianal ulceration.

updates.title: Nicobrevin anti-smoking preparation withdrawn from the market
updates.summary: Risks of Nicobrevin outweigh any benefits.

updates.title: New oral anticoagulants apixaban (Eliquis▼), dabigatran (Pradaxa) and rivaroxaban (Xarelto▼)
updates.summary: Risk of serious haemorrhage—clarified contraindications apply to all 3 medicines.

updates.title: New guidance on reporting suspected adverse drug reactions in children
updates.summary: We are no longer requesting all suspected adverse drug reactions (ADRs) to be reported for children.

updates.title: Natalizumab (Tysabri▼): risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy is increased in patients who have had previous immunosuppressant treatment
updates.summary: Risk of developing progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) associated with natalizumab is increased in patients who have had previous immunosuppressant therapy.

updates.title: Natalizumab (Tysabri▼): risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy increases after 2 years of therapy
updates.summary: The risk of developing progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) with natalizumab increases after 2 years of therapy. Patients with multiple sclerosis should be informed of the risk before treatment, and again after 2 years. The risk of developing PML beyond 3 years of treatment is currently unknown. Product information for healthcare professionals and patients is being updated with the latest information.

updates.title: Mycophenolate mofetil: pure red cell aplasia
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should consider a dose reduction or discontinuation of mycophenolate mofetil if patients develop pure red cell aplasia.

updates.title: Moxifloxacin: increased risk of life-threatening liver reactions and other serious risks
updates.summary: Use in pelvic inflammatory disease only when other antibacterials are inappropriate or ineffective.

updates.title: Monitoring the safety of antiretroviral drugs
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should monitor the use and safety of antiretroviral drugs for the treatment of HIV as they are advanced.

updates.title: Modafinil: restricted use recommended
updates.summary: European Medicines Agency has recommends the use of modafinil should be restricted to treat only sleepiness associated with narcolepsy - should no longer be used for obstructive sleep apnoea or chronic shift work sleep disorder.

updates.title: Modafinil (Provigil): now restricted to narcolepsy
updates.summary: Further information is available to support safer use

updates.title: Metoclopramide: risk of neurological adverse effects
updates.summary: Restricted dose and duration of use.

updates.title: Methysergide: serious fibrotic reactions
updates.summary: Restricted use and new monitoring requirements.

updates.title: Methylthioninium chloride (methylene blue): update on central nervous system (CNS) toxicity
updates.summary: High intravenous doses of methylthioninium chloride (methylene blue) should be avoided for patients being treated with serotonergic antidepressants (eg, SSRIs, clomipramine, and venlafaxine).

updates.title: Methylphenidate: safe and effective use to treat ADHD
updates.summary: Updated guidance to use methylphenidateto safely and effectively for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children of 6 years or older and adolescents.

updates.title: Methylphenidate: new patient information
updates.summary: The design and content of the Patient Information Leaflets for methylphenidate products are being updated with the latest guidance on safe and effective use for patients and carers

updates.title: Mercaptamine and mercaptopurine: confusion between drug names
updates.summary: Prescribers should remain vigilant with regards to the similarity of these 2 drug names.

updates.title: Memantine pump device (Ebixa): risk of medication errors
updates.summary: Differences in dose delivery between the pump device and dropper device for memantine.

updates.title: Mefloquine: strengthened warnings on neuropsychiatric side effects
updates.summary: A recent review of the prescribing information has led to strengthened warnings and new measures to help minimise risks. To minimise the risk of these adverse reactions, mefloquine must not be used for chemoprophylaxis in patients with active or a history of psychiatric disturbances such as depression, anxiety disorders, schizophrenia, or other psychiatric disorders. If neuropsychiatric reactions or changes to mental state occur during mefloquine chemoprophylaxis, the patient should be advised to stop taking mefloquine and seek medical advice as soon as possible so that it can be replaced by another medicine for malaria prevention

updates.title: Medstream Implantable Drug Pumps
updates.summary: Check pumps after MRI.

updates.title: Medical and non-medical prescribing: mixing medicines in clinical practice
updates.summary: Mixing drugs together, where one is not a vehicle for the administration of the other, creates an unlicensed medicine.

updates.title: Lorazepam: reduction of recommended maximum daily dose
updates.summary: Maximum dose of lorazepam for short term, symptomatic treatment is 4 mg per day for severe, disabling anxiety, and 2 mg per day for severe, disabling insomnia

updates.title: Long-acting β-agonists:  use in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
updates.summary: Overall benefits of long-acting β-agonists (LABAs) in the treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) continue to outweigh any risks.

updates.title: Long-acting β2-agonists: reminder for use in children and adults
updates.summary: Benefits of these medicines used in conjunction with inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in the control of asthma symptoms in children outweigh any apparent risks.

updates.title: Liothyronine 20 microgram tablets: continuity of supply and potential need for patient monitoring
updates.summary: Recent interruption to the supply of liothyronine 20 microgram tablets from Amdipharm Mercury.

updates.title: Linezolid: restricted indication
updates.summary: Linezolid is not active against infections caused by Gram-negative pathogens, and treatment should be started only after specialist microbiological advice.

updates.title: Levonorgestrel and ulipristal remain suitable emergency contraceptives for all women
updates.summary: Emergency contraceptives remain suitable for all women regardless of the woman’s weight or body mass index (BMI).

updates.title: Levofloxacin: some indications restricted
updates.summary: Levofloxacin (a fluoroquinolone antibiotic) is unfavourable as first-line treatment for several indications.

updates.title: Lenalidomide: risk of thrombosis and thromboembolism
updates.summary: Patients receiving lenalidomide for management of multiple myeloma should be closely monitored for evidence of arterial and venous thromboembolic events.

updates.title: Lenalidomide (Revlimid▼): update on risk of second primary malignancy
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should consider the possibility of second primary malignancy in patients treated with lenalidomide.

updates.title: Lenalidomide (Revlimid): risk of serious hepatic adverse drug reactions
updates.summary: Routine monitoring of liver function now recommended.

updates.title: Ketoprofen and ketorolac: gastrointestinal risk
updates.summary: Prescribing advice should be followed carefully, particularly recommended upper dose limits due to associated higher gastrointestinal risk than most other NSAIDs in the class.

updates.title: Ivabradine: carefully monitor for bradycardia
updates.summary: Emerging clinical trial evidence of increased cardiovascular risk.

updates.title: Isotretinoin: risk of serious skin reactions
updates.summary: Erythema multiforme, Stevens Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis reported in association with isotretinoin - may result in hospitalisation, disability, life-threatening events, or death.

updates.title: Isotretinoin for severe acne: who should prescribe it
updates.summary: Isotretinoin should only be prescribed by consultant dermatologist-led teams and dispensed only by a hospital pharmacy.

updates.title: Introduction of the Traditional Herbal Registration Certification Mark
updates.summary: A certification mark has been designed and launched as an additional visible symbol.

updates.title: Intravenous zoledronic acid: adverse effects on renal function
updates.summary: Zoledronic acid is associated with reports of renal impairment and renal failure, especially in patients with pre-existing renal dysfunction or other risk factors. Renal function should be measured before each dose, and patients should be adequately hydrated before treatment. Renal function monitoring is recommended after use of zoledronic acid in at-risk patients—especially those with pre-existing renal impairment. Use in patients with severe renal impairment is generally not recommended, but may be considered for tumour-induced hypercalcaemia, if the benefits outweigh the risks.

updates.title: Intravenous paracetamol (Perfalgan ▼): risk of accidental overdose
updates.summary: Risk of accidental overdose, particularly in infants and neonates.

updates.title: Intravenous iron and serious hypersensitivity reactions: strengthened recommendations
updates.summary: New strengthened recommendations to manage and minimise risk.

updates.title: Intravenous iron and serious hypersensitivity reactions
updates.summary: Clarification of advice on new recommendations regarding initial test dose.

updates.title: Intravenous dantrolene: risk of undissolved crystals
updates.summary: Use a filter needle when drawing up reconstituted dantrolene solution.

updates.title: Intravenous 0.18% saline/4% glucose solution (‘hypotonic saline’) in children: reports of fatal hyponatraemia
updates.summary: Do not use in children aged 16 years or less, except in specialist settings under expert medical supervision.

updates.title: Interferon-beta: risk of thrombotic microangiopathy and risk of nephrotic syndrome
updates.summary: There have been reports of thrombotic microangiopathy and nephrotic syndrome linked to interferon beta treatment.

updates.title: Insulin glargine: studies of possible cancer link
updates.summary: The European Medicines Agency has advised that no change in recommendations for use is required at present.

updates.title: Insulin degludec (Tresiba▼): available in additional higher strength
updates.summary: Care needed to minimise risk of error, including training for patients.

updates.title: Insulin combined with pioglitazone: risk of cardiac failure
updates.summary: If pioglitazone is used in combination with insulin patients should be observed for signs and symptoms of heart failure, weight gain, and oedema.

updates.title: Injectable medicines for cosmetic procedures: supply and administration
updates.summary: Updated guidance on the supply and administration of Botox, Vistabel, Dysport, and other injectable medicines used in cosmetic procedures.

updates.title: Inhaled medicines containing corticosteroid
updates.summary: Licensed doses and differences in potency between different inhaled corticosteroids; advice for use with spacer device.

updates.title: Inhaled corticosteroids: pneumonia
updates.summary: Physicians should remain vigilant for pneumonia and other infections of the lower respiratory tract (ie, bronchitis) in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease who are treated with inhaled products that contain steroids

updates.title: Inhaled and intranasal corticosteroids
updates.summary: Risk of psychological and behavioural side effects.

updates.title: Info on progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) from Yellow Card reports
updates.summary: Spontaneous reporting on the Yellow Card portal has provided important information in the identification of PML associated with some drugs.

updates.title: Implanon contraceptive implant: information for women and healthcare professionals
Implanon contraceptive implant: changing to Nexplanon
updates.summary: All healthcare professionals trained in inserting Implanon must make sure they are trained in using Nexplanon before the changeover.

updates.title: Impact of regulatory action taken by MHRA
updates.summary: How MHRA monitors the impact of regulatory action taken.

updates.title: Illegal herbal remedies containing Aristolochia: vigilance needed
updates.summary: MHRA continues to identify cases of herbal medicines, particularly traditional Chinese medicines, which contain illegal and toxic Aristolochia or aristolochic acids.

updates.title: Hydroxyethyl starch intravenous infusion: suspension of licences
updates.summary: Clinical trials have reported an increased risk of renal dysfunction and mortality in critically ill or septic patients who received hydroxyethyl starch (HES) compared with crystalloids.

updates.title: Human papillomavirus vaccine Cervarix: balance of risks and benefits remains clearly positive
updates.summary: A safety review conducted at the end of its routine use during the ongoing human papillomavirus immunisation programme has found that no new risks have been identified for Cervarix, and that the balance of its risks and benefits remains clearly positive. Cervarix was replaced in the programme by the HPV vaccine Gardasil▼ from September 2012.

updates.title: Human papillomavirus immunisation programme
updates.summary: Second year safety review

updates.title: Human papillomavirus (HPV) immunisation programme - first-year safety review
updates.summary: The human papillomavirus (HPV) immunisation programme is now entering its second year and this article summarises the safety experience to date.

updates.title: Hormone-replacement therapy: updated advice
updates.summary: Before prescribing hormone-replacement therapy, healthcare professionals should consider carefully the potential benefits and risks for every woman

updates.title: Hormonal contraceptives: cervical cancer
updates.summary: Latest evidence suggests long-term use of combined oral contraceptives or progestogen-only injectable contraceptives is associated with a small increased risk of cervical cancer.

updates.title: High-dose cyproterone acetate: potential risk of (multiple) meningiomas
updates.summary: Patients with existing meningioma or a history of meningioma must not be prescribed high-dose (≥25 mg per day) cyproterone acetate.

updates.title: Herbal products: safety update
updates.summary: Important to inquire if patients are taking herbal medicines.

updates.title: Herbal product: intensive body lotion with aloe vera contains steroids
updates.summary: MHRA has found samples of intensive body lotion with aloe vera (OSAS) to contain corticosteroid betamethasone.

updates.title: Herbal medicines: new help available when advising patients about safe use
updates.summary: Most herbal medicines on the UK market are currently unlicensed products and it is difficult for consumers or healthcare professionals to identify which products are manufactured to acceptable standards with reliable product information.

updates.title: Herbal ingredient St John’s wort may interact with antiepileptics
updates.summary: Patients with epilepsy should not take products that contain St John’s wort as any antiepileptic medicine may interact with St John’s wort.

updates.title: Glucose solutions: false blood glucose readings when used to flush arterial lines
updates.summary: False blood glucose readings when used to flush arterial lines leading to incorrect insulin administration and potentially fatal hypoglycaemia.

updates.title: Gadolinium-containing contrast agents: new advice to minimise the risk of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
updates.summary: Gadolinium-containing contrast agents are associated with a varying degree of risk of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis. See advice below to minimise risk in the following vulnerable groups: patients with renal impairment; patients in the perioperative liver transplantation period; infants, neonates, and the elderly; and women who are pregnant or breastfeeding. High-risk gadolinium-containing contrast agents are contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment, patients in the perioperative liver-transplantation period, and in neonates

updates.title: Fluoxetine: possible small risk of congenital cardiac defects
updates.summary: Recent epidemiological evidence suggests a possible small increased risk of congenital cardiac defects in association with fluoxetine in early pregnancy, similar to that seen with paroxetine. There are insufficient data to draw conclusions on whether there is a similar risk for other SSRIs. The potential risks should be considered in the context of the benefits of treatment

updates.title: Fingolimod (Gilenya▼): not recommended for patients at known risk of cardiovascular adverse events
updates.summary: New advice for extended early monitoring for those with significant bradycardia or heart block after first dose.

updates.title: Fingolimod (Gilenya▼): bradycardia and heart block
updates.summary: Repeat enhanced cardiovascular monitoring when restarting fingolimod after treatment interruption,

updates.title: Finasteride: potential risk of male breast cancer
updates.summary: Patients should be advised to promptly report to their doctor any changes in their breast tissue such as lumps, pain, or nipple discharge.

updates.title: Filgrastim and pegfilgrastim: risk of capillary leak syndrome
updates.summary: Capillary leak syndrome (CLS) has been reported in recipients of filgrastim, including patients undergoing chemotherapy and a healthy donor undergoing peripheral blood progenitor-cell mobilisation; it has also been reported in recipients of pegfilgrastim undergoing chemotherapy. Episodes varied in severity and frequency. CLS is characterised by: hypotension and oedema; hypoalbuminaemia; and haemoconcentration, and may be fatal unless promptly diagnosed and managed. Prescribers should monitor patients and healthy donors for signs and symptoms of capillary leak syndrome (CLS), and should give standard symptomatic treatment immediately if symptoms occur.

updates.title: Fibrates: first-line treatment not recommended
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should not prescribe them to newly diagnosed patients as first-line treatment, except for those with severe hypertriglyceridaemia or those who cannot take statins.

updates.title: Ferumoxytol: risk of serious hypersensitivity reactions—contraindicated if any drug allergy; administer via infusion
updates.summary: New recommendations are being introduced to minimise the risk of serious hypersensitivity reactions with ferumoxytol.

updates.title: Febuxostat (Adenuric▼): stop treatment if signs or symptoms of serious hypersensitivity
updates.summary: Febuxostat must be stopped immediately if hypersensitivity occurs and must not be re-started in patients who have ever developed a hypersensitivity reaction to febuxostat.

updates.title: Extraneal and products that contain (or are metabolised to) maltose, xylose, or galactose: false blood glucose readings
updates.summary: Patients who use products that contain maltose, xylose, or galactose should use glucose-specific monitors.

updates.title: Exenatide (Byetta ▼): risk of severe pancreatitis and renal failure
updates.summary: There have been reports of necrotising and haemorrhagic pancreatitis in people taking exenatide some of which were fatal - stop exenatide treatment if pancreatitis is diagnosed.

updates.title: Etravirine: reports of severe hypersensitivity reactions
updates.summary: Cases of severe hypersensitivity syndromes, sometimes fatal, have been reported with etravirine.

updates.title: Etoricoxib: prescribing to patients with high blood pressure
updates.summary: Do not prescribe etoricoxib to patients whose blood pressure is persistently above 140/90 mmHg and inadequately controlled.

updates.title: Erlotinib: new safety information
updates.summary: New safety information for intensive monitoring of Erlotinib.

updates.title: Ergot-derived dopamine agonists: risk of fibrotic reactions
updates.summary: New warnings and contraindications for ergot-derived dopamine agonists due to risk of fibrosis associated with chronic use.

updates.title: Ergot-derived dopamine agonists: risk of fibrosis
updates.summary: Do not prescribe ergots to patients who have had fibrosis in the heart, lungs, or abdomen.

updates.title: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitors: serious cases of keratitis and ulcerative keratitis
updates.summary: Patients who present with acute or worsening signs and symptoms of keratitis should be referred promptly to an ophthalmology specialist.

updates.title: Enoxaparin (Clexane) contamination: latest information
updates.summary: Updated information on supply and clinical advice on enoxaparin (Clexane) pre-filled syringes, contaminated with over-sulphated-chondroitin sulphate (OSCS).

updates.title: Ecoflac infusion solutions: risk of air embolism
updates.summary: To avoid the risk of air embolism, these products should not be infused under pressure.

updates.title: Duloxetine: marketed as Cymbalta▼ and Yentreve▼ for different disorders
updates.summary: Patients should be assessed regularly due to reported cases of suicidal ideation and suicidal behaviour during treatment with duloxetine or shortly after stopping treatment.

updates.title: Drugs and driving: clarification for Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland
updates.summary: The new offence introduced in July does not apply in Northern Ireland nor replace any existing offences of driving.

updates.title: Drugs and driving: blood concentration limits to be set for certain controlled drugs in a new legal offence
updates.summary: The Department for Transport has introduced a new offence of driving with certain controlled drugs above specified limits in the blood; this is likely to come into force on 2 March 2015.

updates.title: Drug Safety Update gains NHS Evidence accreditation
updates.summary: NHS Evidence Accreditation Scheme recognises organisations that demonstrate high standards in producing health or social care guidance.

updates.title: Drug alert: recall of Gaviscon Advance Peppermint Flavour, Boots Heartburn Relief Peppermint Flavour, Peptac Peppermint Liquid, and Peptac Liquid Aniseed Flavour
updates.summary: Batches of this medicine are being recalled from the market because of low levels of microbial contamination.

updates.title: Dronedarone (Multaq▼): cardiovascular, hepatic and pulmonary adverse events – new restrictions and monitoring requirements
updates.summary: Following new evidence of cardiovascular, hepatic and pulmonary risk, a review of dronedarone has concluded that the benefits of treatment continue to outweigh the risks for the maintenance of sinus rhythm after successful cardioversion in a limited population of patients with paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation; however, in light of safety concerns dronedarone should only be prescribed after other treatment options have been considered. To support safer use, patients should have their treatment reviewed at the next routine appointment to ensure that they remain eligible for dronedarone treatment according to the revised prescribing information, including new restrictions on use. Regular monitoring of cardiac, liver, and renal function during treatment is recommended

updates.title: Enzira/CSL Biotherapies and Viroflu/Inflexal V influenza vaccines and risk of febrile reactions in children under 5 years
updates.summary: Use alternative vaccines in under 5s and report suspected adverse reactions

updates.title: Dorzolamide hydrochloride/timolol maleate (Cosopt) preservative-free eye drops: new pipette design
updates.summary: Old pipette design withdrawn after reported eye injuries.

updates.title: Doripenem (Doribax▼): updated dosing recommendations
updates.summary: Previous dosing regimens for doripenem in such patients found to be insufficient.

updates.title: Dopamine agonists: pathological gambling, increased libido, and hypersexuality
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals should warn patients that compulsive behaviour with dopamine agonists may be dose-related.

updates.title: Don't miss the latest drug safety advice!
updates.summary: We are changing our arrangements for sending out email alerts about Drug Safety Update.

updates.title: Domperidone: risks of cardiac side effects
updates.summary: Indication restricted to nausea and vomiting, new contraindications, and reduced dose and duration of use.

updates.title: Domperidone: no longer available without prescription
updates.summary: People now need to have a medical assessment before taking domperidone to determine if it is suitable for them due to the risk of cardiac side effects.

updates.title: Dipeptidylpeptidase-4 inhibitors: risk of acute pancreatitis
updates.summary: There have been reports of acute pancreatitis associated with drugs in the dipeptidylpeptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor class of antidiabetic agents (‘gliptins’).

updates.title: Diclofenac: public consultation on availability as a pharmacy medicine
updates.summary: Public consultation launched on the continued availability of oral diclofenac as a pharmacy (P) medicine and on risk-minimisation measures advised by the Commission on Human Medicines.

updates.title: Diclofenac: new contraindications and warnings
updates.summary: New recommendations after a Europe-wide review of cardiovascular safety.

updates.title: Dianeal, Extraneal, and Nutrineal peritoneal dialysis solutions
updates.summary: Risk of aseptic peritonitis with Dianeal, Extraneal, and Nutrineal peritoneal dialysis solutions due to possible presence of endotoxin.

updates.title: Dexrazoxane (Cardioxane): restriction of use
updates.summary: Use restricted to adults with advanced or metastatic breast cancer only.

updates.title: Dexamethasone 4 mg/ml injection (Organon Laboratories Limited): reformulation with changes in name, concentration, storage conditions, and presentation
updates.summary: From October 2014 Dexamethasone 4 mg/ml injection (Organon Laboratories Limited) will be replaced by Dexamethasone 3.8 mg/ml solution for injection (Aspen Pharma Trading Limited).

updates.title: Desmopressin nasal spray: removal of nocturnal enuresis indication
updates.summary: Nasal formulations of desmopressin are no longer indicated for primary nocturnal enuresis.

updates.title: Desmomelt (desmopressin): report incidents on yellow card portal
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals are encouraged to report all suspected adverse reactions (ADRs) on the yellow card porftal to melt formulations of desmopressin.

updates.title: Desiccants in blister packs: reminder of risk of ingestion
updates.summary: Take care to tell people receiving blister packs containing a desiccant that the desiccant should not be swallowed.

updates.title: Denosumab: updated recommendations
updates.summary: Minimising the risk of osteonecrosis of the jaw; monitoring for hypocalcaemia.

updates.title: Denosumab: monitoring recommended
updates.summary: Fatal cases of severe symptomatic hypocalcaemia, and risk of hypocalcaemia at any time during treatment.

updates.title: Denosumab 60 mg (Prolia▼)
updates.summary: Rare cases of atypical femoral fracture with long-term use.

updates.title: Daptomycin: risk of eosinophilic pneumonia
updates.summary: If eosinophilic pneumonia is suspected, daptomycin should be discontinued immediately and if appropriate the patient treated with corticosteroids.

updates.title: Dabigatran (Pradaxa▼): risk of serious haemorrhage
updates.summary: Contraindications clarified and reminder to monitor renal function.

updates.title: Dabigatran (Pradaxa): contraindicated in patients with prosthetic heart valve(s) requiring anti-coagulant treatment
updates.summary: Risk of thrombosis and haemorrhage in patients with prosthetic heart valve(s) requiring anti-coagulant treatment.

updates.title: Cyproterone acetate with ethinylestradiol (co-cyprindiol): balance of benefits and risks remains positive
updates.summary: Updated prescribing advice provided.

updates.title: Counterfeit medicines: what pharmacists should know
updates.summary: How pharmacists can prevent counterfeits reaching patients.

updates.title: Corticosteroids: early psychiatric side-effects
updates.summary: Risk of early psychiatric side-effects is one of several important safety issues for healthcare professionals to discuss with patients and carers, who should seek urgent medical advice in the event of any worrying symptoms.

updates.title: Combined oral contraceptives show they can prevent ovarian cancer
updates.summary: New study shows use of oral contraceptives reduces risk of ovarian cancer.

updates.title: Combined hormonal contraceptives: risk of venous thromboembolism
updates.summary: Non-hormonal or progestogen-only contraception should be considered in some situations.

updates.title: Combined hormonal contraceptives and venous thromboembolism: review confirms risk is small
updates.summary: A review of the latest evidence on the risk of thromboembolism advises to consider risk factors and remain vigilant for signs and symptoms. - the risk of blood clots with all low-dose CHCs is small - there is good evidence that the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) may vary between products, depending on the progestogen - CHCs that contain levonorgestrel, norethisterone, or norgestimate have the lowest risk of VTE - the benefits of any CHC far outweigh the risk of serious side effects - prescribers and women should be aware of the major risk factors for thromboembolism, and of the key signs and symptoms

updates.title: Combination use of medicines from different classes of renin-angiotensin system blocking agents: risk of hyperkalaemia, hypotension, and impaired renal function—new warnings
updates.summary: New warnings due to risk of hyperkalaemia, hypotension, and impaired renal function have been agreed following an EU-wide review.

updates.title: Colobreathe (colistimethate sodium dry powder for inhalation): risk of capsule breakage - new instructions for use
updates.summary: We have received reports of Colobreathe (colistimethate sodium) capsules shattering when pierced by their inhaler device.

updates.title: Colchicine: extremely toxic in overdose
updates.summary: Reminder on risk of serious and fatal toxicity in overdose.

updates.title: Codeine: very rare risk of side-effects in breastfed babies
updates.summary: Breastfed babies might very rarely develop side-effects due to the presence of morphine in breast milk.

updates.title: Codeine: restricted use as analgesic in children and adolescents after European safety review
Codeine for analgesia: restricted use in children because of reports of morphine toxicity
updates.summary: Codeine should only be used to relieve acute moderate pain in children older than 12 years and only if it cannot be relieved by other painkillers such as paracetamol or ibuprofen alone. Furthermore, a significant risk of serious and life-threatening adverse reactions has been identified in children with obstructive sleep apnoea who received codeine after tonsillectomy or adenoidectomy (or both). Codeine is now contraindicated in all children younger than 18 years who undergo these procedures for obstructive sleep apnoea

updates.title: Codeine-containing pain relief in children
updates.summary: Safety review initiated following post-surgical fatalities in ultra-rapid metabolisers

updates.title: Codeine-containing liquid over-the-counter medicines.
updates.summary: Should not be used for cough under 18 years

updates.title: Co-proxamol withdrawal: reminder to prescribers
updates.summary: Co-proxamol's phased withdrawal period lasts until the end of 2007 to enable patients to move to suitable alternatives.

updates.title: Clopidogrel: risk of acquired haemophilia
updates.summary: Reports of acquired haemophilia have been received in association with clopidogrel.

updates.title: Clopidogrel and proton pump inhibitors: interaction—updated advice
updates.summary: In light of the most recent evidence, the previous advice on the concomitant use of clopidogrel with proton pump inhibitors has now been modified. Use of either omeprazole or esomeprazole with clopidogrel should be discouraged. The current evidence does not support extending this advice to other PPIs

updates.title: Clarification: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor antagonists
updates.summary: Use during breastfeeding

updates.title: Citalopram and escitalopram: QT interval prolongation
updates.summary: New maximum daily dose restrictions (including in elderly patients), contraindications, and warnings.

updates.title: Cilostazol (Pletal): risks of cardiovascular and bleeding events
updates.summary: Indication restricted to second-line treatment and contraindicated with some cardiovascular conditions and medicines Furthermore, cilostazol is now contraindicated in patients with any of the following: Unstable angina, recent myocardial infarction or coronary intervention (within 6 months) a history of severe tachyarrhythmia those receiving two or more other antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatments For patients starting cilostazol, prescribers should assess benefit after 3 months of treatment, and should stop treatment if patients have not made clinically relevant improvements in walking distance. All patients who are currently receiving long-term treatment should be reassessed at a routine appointment, in light of the new advice.

updates.title: Chlorhexidine solutions: reminder of the risk of chemical burns in premature infants
updates.summary: A European review has considered MHRA evidence together with additional information from spontaneous reporting and published literature.

updates.title: Chlorhexidine: reminder of potential for hypersensitivity
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals are reminded that chlorhexidine is known to induce hypersensitivity, including generalised allergic reactions and anaphylactic shock.

updates.title: Chloral hydrate (Welldorm) and Triclofos
updates.summary: These medicines are not first-line options for insomnia.

updates.title: Cetuximab: new safety information available
updates.summary: importance of establishing wild type RAS (KRAS and NRAS) status before treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer

updates.title: Central alerting system (CAS): access to urgent safety guidance
updates.summary: Use the central alerting system to view and search new alerts, as well as past alerts that were issued through the public health link and safety alert broadcast system.

updates.title: Ceftriaxone (rocephin): incompatible with solutions containing calcium
updates.summary: Updated advice for healthcare professionals not to mix or infuse ceftriaxone with solutions containing calcium.

updates.title: Carisoprodol and meprobamate: risks outweigh benefits
updates.summary: Marketing authorisations for carisoprodol are to be suspended after a European review concluded that the risks of treatment outweigh the benefits.

updates.title: Carbapenems: concomitant use with valproic acid not recommended
updates.summary: A clinically significant interaction between carbapenems and valproic acid results in reduced valproate plasma concentrations with potential for inadequate seizure control. Concomitant use of these agents is not recommended, and healthcare professionals should consider alternative antibacterial therapy

updates.title: Carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine and eslicarbazepine: potential risk of serious skin reactions
updates.summary: Risk of serious skin-related adverse drug reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, occurring with carbamazepine may be increased in the presence of the HLA-A*3101 allele in patients of European descent or Japanese origin.

updates.title: Capecitabine: risk of severe skin reactions - discontinue treatment
updates.summary: Severe skin reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported during treatment with capecitabine.

updates.title: Calcium gluconate injection in small-volume glass containers: new contraindications due to aluminium exposure risk
updates.summary: Aluminium can be leached from glass after contact with calcium gluconate solution, leading to a risk of exposure to aluminium. Accumulation of aluminium might have adverse effects on bone mineralisation and neurological development in children and those with renal impairment. Calcium gluconate injection packed in small-volume glass containers is now contraindicated for use as repeated or prolonged treatment, including as an intravenous infusion, in children younger than 18 years and in patients with renal impairment. To limit the exposure of patients to aluminium, especially in those with impaired renal function and in children, calcium gluconate injection in small-volume glass containers is also contraindicated in the preparation of total parenteral nutrition solutions. Use of calcium gluconate injection packed in plastic containers is recommended to reduce aluminium burden in vulnerable patients

updates.title: Calcium and vitamin D: no prescribing changes
updates.summary: Studies of cardiovascular risk don’t support prescribing changes.

updates.title: Calcitonin (Miacalcic): increased risk of cancer with long-term use
updates.summary: Calcitonin-containing medicines should no longer be used in treatment of osteoporosis.

updates.title: Caffeine for apnoea of prematurity
updates.summary: All products to be named and prescribed as caffeine citrate.

updates.title: Caffeine citrate: 2 products of different strengths now available
updates.summary: Care must be taken with dosing as the 2 products are not equivalent.

updates.title: Cabazitaxel (Jevtana▼): risk of medication error resulting in overdose
updates.summary: It is essential that the entire contents of the solvent vial is added to the concentrate vial to produce a concentrate-solvent mixture with the intended concentration of 10 mg/mL cabazitaxel. It is essential that the entire contents of the solvent vial is added to the concentrate vial to produce a concentrate-solvent mixture with the intended concentration of 10 mg/mL cabazitaxel Pharmacies should review worksheets used in the preparation of cabazitaxel to ensure that they inform pharmacy staff to add the entire contents of the solvent vial to the concentrate vial

updates.title: Buccal midazolam (Buccolam▼): new authorised medicine for paediatric use
updates.summary: Care needed when transferring from unlicensed formulations.

updates.title: Botulinum toxin type B (Neurobloc): serious known risks
updates.summary: Risks such as toxin spread reported mostly with off-label use.

updates.title: Botulinum toxin products: rare but serious risks
updates.summary: Products that contain botulinum toxin are associated with the risk of serious adverse reactions due to distant spread of toxin.

updates.title: Boceprevir (Victrelis) and telaprevir (Incivo): predictive factors for sepsis, worsening liver function, and mortality
updates.summary: A European review identified baseline markers as predictive factors for morbidity requiring hospitalisation and mortality in cirrhotic patients.

updates.title: Blue dyes: risk of serious allergic reactions
updates.summary: Surgeons reminded to have competent personnel and emergency facilities available for at least 1 hour after administration of the blue dye.

updates.title: Black Triangle (▼) medicines part of an EU-wide scheme
updates.summary: Remember to report any suspected adverse reactions

updates.title: Bivalirudin: risks associated with incorrect dose
updates.summary: Incorrect dosage of bivalirudin in percutaneous coronary intervention can lead to major adverse cardiac events.

updates.title: Bisphosphonates: osteonecrosis of the jaw
updates.summary: All patients with cancer should have a dental check-up before bisphosphonate treatment.

updates.title: Bisphosphonates: atypical femoral fractures
updates.summary: Atypical femoral fractures reported rarely with bisphosphonate therapy, mainly in patients receiving long-term treatment for osteoporosis.

updates.title: Bisphosphonates: atrial fibrillation
